doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Music in the house and early interest in how records were made
summary: Rudy says there was always music at home and that as a teenager he wanted to know how records were made.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You were born in New Jersey. Was there music in your house when you were growing up via the radio, or anything?

Always music, yes. Radio, records, and even my parents were in to music. On my father’s side, they were always musical, they always had a piano at home, and all my friends were interested in the kind of music that was happening.
So when did you get interested in recording?

Well that was all my adult life actually. [My] teenage years, I was always interested in how records were made, I was always interested in the aspect of musicians, and playing what the music was. My friends were the same way. I used to go to the record store and buy records, go home, and figure out how they made them.
